sourceBlocks.heading: City trees: what one street can do
sourceBlocks.text: A practice deck written for this repository. The numbers are examples for a school project, not measurements.

sourceBlocks.heading: The question
sourceBlocks.text:
Can a single row of street trees make a hot street noticeably cooler in summer?
The class measured one street with trees and one without, 300 metres apart.

sourceBlocks.heading: How the class measured
sourceBlocks.text:
Two thermometers at a height of 1.5 metres, read every hour from 10:00 to 18:00.
Measured on 12 sunny days in July.
Both streets have the same width and the same dark asphalt.

sourceBlocks.heading: The result
sourceBlocks.text:
At 15:00 the street without trees reached 34 °C on average.
The street with trees reached 31 °C at the same time.
The difference was largest in the afternoon and close to zero at 10:00 in the morning.

sourceBlocks.heading: Why shade is not the whole story
sourceBlocks.text:
Leaves also release water, which cools the air around them.
On the 2 days after rain the difference grew from 3 °C to 4 °C.

sourceBlocks.heading: Limits
sourceBlocks.text:
Only two streets were compared, so other differences between them may play a role.
The class did not measure at night, when trees can hold warm air under their crowns.

sourceBlocks.heading: Takeaway
sourceBlocks.text:
One row of trees made the afternoon about 3 °C cooler on this street.
The effect depends on water: trees that are dry cool less.
